text: The dark-matter paper T14 fixes how much matter each dark tower holds. By its unit-ball rule the mirror carries 18.6 percent of the dark matter, the three-dimensional towers 49.7 percent and the five-dimensional towers 31.6 percent. This note sets out the assumptions, equations, code and results of the tests of those amounts. Quanta confined to a sheet scatter in two dimensions; per unit of the mass gravity sees, their cross-section is a length times the sheet spacing. At composite strength the three-dimensional towers' matter is a fluid, eight to thirteen orders of magnitude above the cluster bound, whatever its confinement scale. A tree-gravity, multi-species smoothed-particle code, with the sheet fluid's pressure confined to its planes, follows a Bullet-like merger and a cluster's assembly. As T14 writes it, the composition fails both tests: 68 percent of the dark matter collides, with randomly oriented sheets the subcluster dissolves from the lensing map, and halos reach about 0.4 of the cold-dark-matter ellipticity. If the odd towers' matter is collisionless, only the mirror collides; the subcluster keeps a lensing peak on its galaxies, its gas trailing, at the cost of a puffier subcluster and halos about 0.8 as elliptical. A semi-analytic Milky Way model with helium-star feedback excludes the mirror's proton-only branch; its helium branch fits at the Sun under some normalisations, and in the bulge only if the bulge holds over twice the mirror's proportional share of its dark mass. Two films, the code and a verification script accompany the note.

title: R1: equal mass per quantum
text: The quanta of every populated tower carry the same mass $m$.

title: R2: one quantum per unit ball
text: A populated tower whose space has $D$ dimensions ($2$, $3$ or $4$) holds one quantum per unit ball $\B^{D}$ of that space, in one unit of length common to all towers: every tower has the same Wigner-Seitz radius. The rule presupposes that all six towers are populated, which for the odd four is the inference of Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}.

title: R3: one cell per unshared direction
text: In the sourcing rule, a tower's matter counts through exactly one cell radius of each direction its neighbour lacks, on one side: a five-dimensional tower's matter through one radius of its extra direction, and a three-dimensional tower's sheets stacked one radius apart along the direction it lacks. the section ``The thickness: a contact mechanism'' gives a mechanism that returns this value and costs it.

title: C: the odd towers collisionless
text: The matter of the four odd towers (the two three-dimensional and the two five-dimensional towers) has no self-interaction of order one. For the three-dimensional towers this means an in-sheet s-wave phase shift below about $2 \times 10^{-7}$ at cluster speeds for isotropic compression, $4 \times 10^{-6}$ for compression normal to the sheets (Corollary \claimref{simulations.confinement-scale-does-not-matter}).

title: S1: one species per tower
text: The matter of each populated tower is one species. Within its tower it is either collisionless or a fluid; across towers species interact only through gravity (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}). Our matter is two species: galaxies, collisionless, and our gas.

title: S2: the sheet fluid
text: At composite strength the three-dimensional towers' matter is an ideal gas with two degrees of freedom ($\gamma = 2$) whose pressure and viscosity act only within its sheet. Along the sheet's normal it moves without pressure, since sheets cross freely \cite[Rem.~7.30]{ButlerT14}. The sheets of a given orientation form one family shared by all the matter of the tower \cite[Lem.~6.1, Prem.~7.4]{ButlerT14}, so parcels of different halos on the same sheet collide. T14 does not say how quanta on differently oriented sheets interact; between two such parcels the force and separation are contracted with the mean of the two in-plane projectors, $(P_{i} + P_{j})/2$, which is the projection onto the sheet when the normals are parallel and otherwise keeps a fraction of each normal component (Lemma \claimref{simulations.averaged-pair-operator}).

title: S3: the mirror in a cluster
text: Mirror matter in a cluster is a fully ionised helium plasma, $\gamma = 5/3$, cooling by bremsstrahlung alone (below about $10^{6}$ K He$^{+}$ line cooling would in reality dominate, so settling would come sooner; Cost K3). Gas that cools below about $7 \times 10^{4}$ K becomes collisionless (the settled phase). There is no mirror star formation and no feedback.

title: S4: our matter
text: Our gas is adiabatic, $\gamma = 5/3$, without cooling. Galaxies are collisionless particles carrying $2$ percent of each halo's mass. They are stellar-mass tracers on galaxy scales (each carries $10^{10}$ to $4 \times 10^{10}\ \Msun$), not galaxies with internal structure.

title: S5: halos
text: Each halo is a Hernquist sphere matched to a Navarro-Frenk-White halo of the same mass and concentration, in equilibrium, with every species sharing the profile in proportion to its mass fraction.

title: Introduction
text:
The dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14} derives eight towers of the Clifford clock, proves that matter in the five populated dark towers gravitates on our metric and does nothing else, and by one geometric rule, the unit-ball rule, returns the ratio of dark to visible matter as $(11\pi + 16)/(3\pi) = 5.364$. The Clifford clock is the mod-$8$ periodicity of the real Clifford algebras, read as a ladder of spacetimes of different dimension, ours among them. The rule was found by fitting one length, so the total is not a test of it. What the rule also fixes, and what can be tested, is the composition: which towers hold how much, and therefore what that matter does when halos collide, when clusters assemble and when gas settles into a galaxy.

Tower dimensions count time. A three-dimensional tower has two space dimensions, so its matter lives on sheets, one direction short of ours; a five-dimensional tower has four, one more. There are two of each, and these four are the odd towers; with the mirror, a copy of ours, they are the five populated dark towers. The share of a tower is the ratio of unit-ball volumes, $V_{3}/V_{D}$ for a tower whose space has $D$ dimensions, which gives $V_{3}/V_{2} = 4/3$ for each three-dimensional tower (Fact \claimref{simulations.imported-unit-ball-rule-family}).

This note collects everything that was done to test the composition. It is a methods note: each section states its premises, the equations it uses, how the code implements them, and what came out. Nothing here changes a derived result of T14. Where the tests disagree with a physical statement of T14, the note says which statement and what was found, and T14 records the outcome in its Section 7.7.

title: Imported: the unit-ball rule and its family
text:
Under Premises R1 (equal mass per quantum), R2 (one quantum per unit ball of each tower's space, with a common Wigner-Seitz radius $d_{b}$) and R3 (one cell radius per unshared direction), the share of a tower whose space has $D$ dimensions is $V_{3}/V_{D}$, and
\[
\frac{\Omega_{\mathrm{dark}}}{\Omega_{b}} \;=\; 1 + 2\cdot\frac{4}{3} + 2\cdot\frac{8}{3\pi} \;=\; \frac{11\pi + 16}{3\pi} \;=\; 5.364 .
\]
With the thickness of the unshared direction left as $c\,d_{b}$ the total is
\[
T(c) \;=\; 1 + \frac{8}{3c} + \frac{16c}{3\pi},
\]

title: Imported: the mirror
text: The mirror tower is a copy of ours, populated at $\Omega_{b'} = 0.995$ to $1$ times $\Omega_{b}$ where its matter is helium or protons. Its temperature ratio $\xi = T'/T$ lies between the gravitational floor, $2.8$ to $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$, and the hot-deposit estimate, about $4 \times 10^{-3}$, a free datum of the descent that is an exception to P2 (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2}); its baryon-to-photon ratio is $\eta' = \eta/\xi^{3}$. T14 takes it to be helium on the expected (burning) branch and protons on the alternative; T14c finds it helium for $\xi$ between about $3 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2 \times 10^{-2}$, an interval containing the hot-deposit estimate, and at the floor degenerate and, for a copied lepton number $L \leq 0$, $96$ to $100$ percent neutrons (Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition}). As neutral atoms its elastic cross-section per mass is of order $2 \times 10^{8}$ (hydrogen) or $5 \times 10^{7}$ (helium) $\cmg$, and inside a halo it is a plasma, collisional and dissipative like our gas. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thm.~4.3, Props.~4.6 and 4.7, Prop.~6.2]{ButlerT14}.

title: Imported from the dark-matter paper
text:
Throughout, the dark composition at $c = 1$ is
\begin{equation}
f_{\mathrm{mirror}} = \frac{3\pi}{11\pi + 16} = 0.1864,\qquad
f_{3\mathrm{D}} = \frac{8\pi}{11\pi + 16} = 0.4971,\qquad
f_{5\mathrm{D}} = \frac{16}{11\pi + 16} = 0.3165,
\end{equation}
and the baryon fraction of every halo is $1/(1 + T) = 0.1571$. Each tower's matter makes up these fractions of the dark matter in every halo; the cosmic baryon fraction is taken as the rule's $1/(1 + T) = 0.1571$ in the simulations and as Planck's $\Omega_{b}/\Omega_{m} = 0.1565$ in the Galaxy model (whose $H_{0}$ is $67.4$ km/s/Mpc; the simulations use $70$ in $r_{200}$). The mixed count of T14 \cite[Rem.~7.10]{ButlerT14} exchanges $f_{3\mathrm{D}}$ and $f_{5\mathrm{D}}$ and has the same total, since $T(\pi/2) = T(1)$. T14 records it as an assignment that is not consistent; it is run alongside as a comparison.

title: Imported: the Bullet Cluster
text: In 1E0657-558 the two galaxy concentrations are $0.72$ Mpc apart on the sky; the lensing peaks lie $9.6''$ ($42$ kpc, subcluster) and $11.8''$ ($52$ kpc, main cluster) from the brightest cluster galaxies, within $1\sigma$ of the galaxy luminosity centroids, and the centres of total mass are offset from the plasma at $8\sigma$ \cite{Clowe2006}. The mass-to-light ratios give $(M/L)_{\mathrm{sub}}/(M/L)_{\mathrm{main}} = 0.84 \pm 0.07$, from which the subcluster has lost no more than about $23$ percent of its mass (a bound on mass loss inferred from the ratio, not on the mass inside a fixed aperture). title: The premises of this note
text: The simulations need a model of each tower's matter that T14 does not supply. These are the premises, stated once and used throughout.

title: The effective cross-section
text: A quantum of a three-dimensional tower lives in a two-dimensional sheet. It collides only with quanta of its own sheet, and its cross-section is a length $\lambda$. Gravity sees the tower's matter per unit of shared three-volume \cite[Lem.~6.1]{ButlerT14}.

title: The effective cross-section of sheet matter
text:
Let the sheets carry $n_{2}$ quanta per unit area, be stacked a distance $s$ apart, and let each quantum have in-sheet cross-section $\lambda$. Then the collision rate of a quantum moving at speed $v$ equals that of a three-dimensional gas of number density $n_{3} = n_{2}/s$ with cross-section
\[
\sigma_{\mathrm{eff}} \;=\; \lambda\, s ,
\qquad\text{so}\qquad
\frac{\sigma_{\mathrm{eff}}}{m} \;=\; \frac{\lambda s}{m}.
\]
In a halo region of overdensity $\Delta$ at redshift $z$ the spacing lies between $d_{b}\Delta^{-1}/(1+z)$ (all compression along the normal) and $d_{b}/(1+z)$ (all compression in the plane), and is $s = d_{b}\Delta^{-1/3}/(1+z)$ for isotropic compression.
proof: The in-sheet collision rate is $n_{2}\lambda v$, and $n_{2}\lambda v = (n_{2}/s)(\lambda s)v = n_{3}\sigma_{\mathrm{eff}}v$. By R3 (\claimref{dark-matter.r3-one-cell-per-unshared-direction}) the sheets are $d_{b}$ apart in the mean, comoving \cite[Prem.~7.4]{ButlerT14}. A region compressed by $\Delta$ in volume has its comoving lengths reduced by $\Delta$ along one direction, by $\Delta^{1/3}$ along each for isotropic compression, or not at all along the normal if the compression is in the plane; the physical spacing carries the further factor $1/(1+z)$.

title: The effective cross-section
Imported: low-energy scattering in two dimensions
text: For elastic scattering in two dimensions by a hard disk of radius $a$, the partial-wave phase shifts are $\tan\delta_{m} = J_{m}(ka)/Y_{m}(ka)$ and the total cross-section is the length $\lambda = (4/k)\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty}\sin^{2}\delta_{m}$. As $ka \to 0$ only $m = 0$ survives, with $\delta_{0} \to \pi/\bigl(2(\ln(ka/2) + \gamma_{E})\bigr)$; the same logarithmic form holds for any short-range interaction with two-dimensional scattering length of order $a$. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{Adhikari1986}.
provenance: S. K. Adhikari, Quantum scattering in two dimensions, Am. J. Phys. 54 (1986) 362.

title: The cluster bound in two dimensions
proof:
Follows from \claimref{simulations.imported-low-energy-scattering-two-dimensions} and \claimref{simulations.effective-cross-section-sheet-matter}, as the source states.

The computation rests on \claimref{dark-matter.r1-equal-mass-per-quantum} and \claimref{dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball}, which fix the isotropic spacing of a cluster core used in (ii): one quantum of the common mass per unit ball of the common length.

title: The confinement scale drops out
text: \textbf{How it is computed.} (i) is Fact \claimref{simulations.imported-low-energy-scattering-two-dimensions} evaluated at $ka = 0.0050$ and $ka = 2.4 \times 10^{-13}$, with $\mu = m/2$; the script computes the Bessel functions by their series and the partial-wave sum to $m = \pm 1$. (ii) is Proposition \claimref{simulations.effective-cross-section-sheet-matter} with $s = 3.5$ cm solved for $\lambda$. (iii) With the s-wave alone $\lambda = 4\sin^{2}\delta_{0}/k$, so $\lambda < 4.8 \times 10^{-12}$ fm gives $\delta_{0} < 1.7 \times 10^{-7}$; in the logarithmic form $\lambda \approx \pi^{2}/\bigl(k(\ln(ka/2) + \gamma_{E})^{2}\bigr)$, so the bound requires $|\ln(ka/2) + \gamma_{E}| > 9.3 \times 10^{6}$, that is $a < 10^{-4.0 \times 10^{6}}$ fm. These are floating-point evaluations, checked in the script (the section ``Machine verification''); nothing below depends on their digits beyond the first.

title: The confinement scale does not matter
text: Any self-interaction of composite strength makes the three-dimensional towers' matter a fluid in clusters, whatever the size of a composite. The cluster bound is met only if the quanta barely interact: an in-sheet phase shift below about $2 \times 10^{-7}$ (isotropic compression in a core; about $4 \times 10^{-6}$ for compression normal to the sheets), which is Premise C.
proof: For $\lambda \ge 0.21$ fm, the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.effective-cross-section-sheet-matter} gives $\sigma_{\mathrm{eff}}/m \ge 9.5 \times 10^{7}\ \cmg$ in every cluster region and compression. Smaller composites barely lower this: a hard disk of radius $a = 10^{-30}$ fm still has $\lambda \approx \pi^{2}/\{k\,[\ln(ka/2) + \gamma_{E}]^{2}\} \approx 0.08$ fm (with $\ln(ka/2) = -73.5$; by \claimref{simulations.imported-low-energy-scattering-two-dimensions}), so $\sigma_{\mathrm{eff}}/m \ge 3 \times 10^{7}\ \cmg$ (by \claimref{simulations.effective-cross-section-sheet-matter}), and the matter remains a fluid on cluster scales. The size of a composite enters $\lambda$ only through the logarithm (Computation \claimref{simulations.cluster-bound-two-dimensions}(i) and (iii)), so no physical confinement scale reaches the bound. The phase-shift limits are Computation \claimref{simulations.cluster-bound-two-dimensions}(iii) at the isotropic spacing and, since $\lambda \propto \sin^{2}\delta_{0}$ and the bound on $\lambda$ scales as $1/s$, a factor $(4.4 \times 10^{10}/9.5 \times 10^{7})^{1/2} \approx 22$ larger at the normal-compression spacing.

title: The confinement scale drops out
text: \textbf{The five-dimensional towers and the mirror.} A five-dimensional tower's matter counts through one cell radius $L$ of its extra direction, so its effective cross-section is $\sigma_{4}/L$ with $\sigma_{4} \sim \lambda^{3}$; in general $\sigma_{\mathrm{eff}} = \sigma_{D}\,d_{b}^{\,3-D}$. For $\lambda = 0.21$ to $2$ fm and $L = d_{b}/(1+z)$ this is $7 \times 10^{-20}$ to $6 \times 10^{-17}\ \cmg$: collisionless by geometry. The mirror's figure is that of Fact \claimref{simulations.imported-mirror}, $5 \times 10^{7}$ to $2 \times 10^{8}\ \cmg$: a fluid like our gas. a figure of the original shows the three.

title: The colliding share
text:
If collisional dark matter were held back in a merger as completely as the gas is, the share of the dark matter that collides would bound the subcluster's mass loss, whatever its cross-section. As a heuristic, then, by the relation displayed with \claimref{simulations.imported-mirror}:
\[
\text{(W): } f_{\mathrm{mirror}} + f_{3\mathrm{D}} = 68.3\%, \qquad
\text{(C): } f_{\mathrm{mirror}} = 18.6\%, \qquad
\text{mixed count: } 50.3\%,
\]
against a mass loss of at most $23$ percent (Fact \claimref{simulations.imported-bullet-cluster}). These are shares of the dark matter, as T14 counts them, so the bound is read as a bound on the subcluster's dark matter, its gas having been stripped in any case. Counted with the subcluster's own gas ($13.7$ percent of its mass: the baryon fraction $0.157$ less the $2$ percent in galaxies), the colliding fraction of its mass is $0.137 + 0.843\,f$, with $f$ the colliding share of the dark matter above: $71$ percent in (W), $29$ in (C) and $56$ in the mixed count, and on that count reading (C) is above the bound as well. T14 \cite[Rem.~7.10, Prop.~7.15(v)]{ButlerT14} counts the self-interacting fraction as the three-dimensional towers alone (about half) and tests the mirror's $18.6$ percent separately; for a bound on mass loss the two add. The simulations of the section ``Results: mergers and halos'' test the heuristic, and it holds only roughly in either direction: colliding matter that partly passes through is held back less than its share (\texttt{rule\_par}), while a halo that puffs loses more than its share from a fixed aperture (Observation \claimref{simulations.merger}). a figure of the original shows the comparison.

title: The simulation code
text: The code \file{tpsim.c} \cite{ButlerSuppT14b} was written for these tests, in C with OpenMP. It solves gravity for every particle and smoothed-particle hydrodynamics separately for each fluid species, so that each fluid interacts hydrodynamically only with itself (Premise S1).

title: Units and species
Gravity
text:
Gravity is computed with a Barnes-Hut octree \cite{BarnesHut1986}. A node of side $\ell$ at distance $r$ from its centre of mass is opened if $\ell^{2} > \theta^{2}r^{2}$ or if the particle lies inside it, with $\theta = 0.7$. Forces use Plummer softening,
\[
\mathbf{a}_{i} \;=\; \sum_{j} G\,m_{j}\,\frac{\mathbf{r}_{j} - \mathbf{r}_{i}}{\bigl(|\mathbf{r}_{j} - \mathbf{r}_{i}|^{2} + \epsilon^{2}\bigr)^{3/2}},
\qquad \epsilon = 15\ \kpc ,
\]
with nodes standing in for the particles they contain.

title: Smoothed-particle hydrodynamics
text:
Each fluid species has its own tree. The kernel is the cubic spline of support $2h$ \cite{MonaghanLattanzio1985},
\[
W(r, h) = \frac{1}{\pi h^{3}}
\begin{cases}
1 - \tfrac{3}{2}q^{2} + \tfrac{3}{4}q^{3}, & 0 \le q < 1,\\[2pt]
\tfrac{1}{4}(2 - q)^{3}, & 1 \le q < 2,\\[2pt]
0, & q \ge 2,
\end{cases}
\qquad q = r/h ,
\]
normalised so that $\int W\,d^{3}r = 1$. Density is gathered at each particle's own smoothing length, $\rho_{i} = \sum_{j} m_{j}W(r_{ij}, h_{i})$; pressure and sound speed are $P_{i} = (\gamma - 1)\rho_{i}u_{i}$ and $c_{i} = \sqrt{\gamma(\gamma - 1)u_{i}}$. The next smoothing length is
\[
h_{i} = \tfrac{1}{2}\Bigl(\frac{3N_{\mathrm{ngb}}m_{i}}{4\pi\rho_{i}}\Bigr)^{1/3}, \qquad N_{\mathrm{ngb}} = 40,
\]
limited to a change between $0.8$ and $1.25$ per step, floored at $h_{\min} = 10\ \kpc$, and cut to $0.7h_{i}$ if a particle's neighbour list reaches its cap of $2000$.

The equations of motion are the symmetric form \cite{Monaghan1992},
\begin{align*}
\frac{d\mathbf{v}_{i}}{dt} &= -\sum_{j} m_{j}\Bigl(\frac{P_{i}}{\rho_{i}^{2}} + \frac{P_{j}}{\rho_{j}^{2}} + \Pi_{ij}\Bigr)\,\mathbf{g}_{ij},
\\
\frac{du_{i}}{dt} &= \sum_{j} m_{j}\Bigl(\frac{P_{i}}{\rho_{i}^{2}} + \tfrac{1}{2}\Pi_{ij}\Bigr)\,\mathbf{v}_{ij}\cdot\mathbf{g}_{ij},
\end{align*}
with the kernel gradient averaged over the two smoothing lengths, $\mathbf{g}_{ij} = \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(\nabla_{i}W(r_{ij}, h_{i}) + \nabla_{i}W(r_{ij}, h_{j})\bigr)$, and $\mathbf{v}_{ij} = \mathbf{v}_{i} - \mathbf{v}_{j}$. The artificial viscosity acts on approaching pairs \cite{MonaghanGingold1983}:
\[
\Pi_{ij} = \frac{-\alpha\,\bar{c}_{ij}\mu_{ij} + \beta\mu_{ij}^{2}}{\bar{\rho}_{ij}}, \qquad
\mu_{ij} = \frac{\bar{h}_{ij}\,\mathbf{v}_{ij}\cdot\mathbf{r}_{ij}}{r_{ij}^{2} + 0.01\bar{h}_{ij}^{2}} \quad (\mathbf{v}_{ij}\cdot\mathbf{r}_{ij} < 0),
\]
with $\alpha = 1$, $\beta = 2$ and bars denoting pair means. Internal energy is floored at $u_{\mathrm{floor}} = u(10^{4}\ \mathrm{K})$ for mean particle mass $0.6\,m_{p}$.

title: The sheet fluid
text:
Premise S2 is implemented by contracting both the kernel gradient and the separation vector of every pair of sheet-fluid particles with an averaged pair operator before they enter the equations above. With $\mathbf{n}_{i}$ and $\mathbf{n}_{j}$ the unit normals of the two particles' sheets,
\begin{equation}
P_{ij} \;=\; I - \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(\mathbf{n}_{i}\mathbf{n}_{i}^{\mathsf T} + \mathbf{n}_{j}\mathbf{n}_{j}^{\mathsf T}\bigr),
\qquad
\mathbf{g}_{ij} \mapsto P_{ij}\mathbf{g}_{ij}, \quad \mathbf{r}_{ij} \mapsto P_{ij}\mathbf{r}_{ij}.
\end{equation}
$P_{ij}$ is the mean of the two in-plane projectors $I - \mathbf{n}_{i}\mathbf{n}_{i}^{\mathsf T}$ and $I - \mathbf{n}_{j}\mathbf{n}_{j}^{\mathsf T}$. When all normals are parallel it is the projection onto the common sheet, nothing acts along the normal except gravity, and motion along it is ballistic; for differently oriented normals it is not a projection and keeps part of each normal component (Lemma \claimref{simulations.averaged-pair-operator}(iii)). Each particle's normal is fixed at its initial value, random per particle or common to all (the section ``Initial conditions'').

title: The averaged pair operator
proof: (i) $P_{ij}$ is symmetric in $i$ and $j$ and $\mathbf{g}_{ij} = -\mathbf{g}_{ji}$, so the force of $j$ on $i$, $-m_{i}m_{j}F_{ij}P_{ij}\mathbf{g}_{ij}$ with $F_{ij}$ the symmetric bracket, is minus the force of $i$ on $j$. The kinetic power of the pair is $-m_{i}m_{j}F_{ij}\,\mathbf{v}_{ij}\cdot P_{ij}\mathbf{g}_{ij}$, and the two internal-energy terms sum to $+m_{i}m_{j}F_{ij}\,\mathbf{v}_{ij}\cdot P_{ij}\mathbf{g}_{ij}$, since $\mathbf{v}_{ji}\cdot P_{ji}\mathbf{g}_{ji} = \mathbf{v}_{ij}\cdot P_{ij}\mathbf{g}_{ij}$ and the viscous term is split equally. (ii) With $Q(\mathbf{n}) = \mathbf{n}\mathbf{n} = 1$ (\claimref{std-algebra.vector-squares}) and $\mathbf{v}\mathbf{n} = \mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n} + \mathbf{v}\wedge\mathbf{n}$ (\claimref{std-algebra.product-decomposition}), $(\mathbf{v}\wedge\mathbf{n})\mathbf{n} = (\mathbf{v}\mathbf{n} - \mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n})\mathbf{n} = \mathbf{v} - (\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n})\mathbf{n} = (I - \mathbf{n}\mathbf{n}^{\mathsf T})\mathbf{v}$. (iii) For $\mathbf{n}_{i}\perp\mathbf{n}_{j}$, $P_{ij}\mathbf{n}_{i} = \tfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{n}_{i}$, $P_{ij}\mathbf{n}_{j} = \tfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{n}_{j}$ and $P_{ij}$ fixes $\mathbf{n}_{i}\times\mathbf{n}_{j}$, so $P_{ij}^{2} \ne P_{ij}$; in general $P_{ij}$ is idempotent only when $\mathbf{n}_{i}\mathbf{n}_{i}^{\mathsf T} = \mathbf{n}_{j}\mathbf{n}_{j}^{\mathsf T}$. Not covered by (i): variable smoothing lengths without correction terms, and what acts after these equations (the integrator, the energy floor and cooling). The script checks (i) on a rational instance with distinct normals and viscosity, (ii) exactly in the blade engine, and (iii) in exact rationals.

title: The sheet fluid
text: The averaging in the relation displayed with \claimref{simulations.confinement-scale-does-not-matter} is an approximation: it stands in for the interaction of quanta on differently oriented sheets, which T14 does not specify (Premise S2). The runs with all sheets parallel (the section ``Initial conditions'') do not use the average. With the normals along the line of sight (\texttt{rule\_perp}) the subcluster fails as with random sheets; with the normals along the merger axis (\texttt{rule\_par}) the fluid slides through along the axis and the subcluster keeps a lensing peak but half its mass (the section ``Results: mergers and halos'').

title: The mirror's cooling and settling
text:
Bremsstrahlung from a fully ionised helium plasma, with Gaunt factor $1.2$ and $Z^{2} = 4$, gives $du/dt = -A\rho\sqrt{u}$ for a constant $A$. At fixed density this has the exact solution
\[
\sqrt{u(t + \Delta t)} \;=\; \sqrt{u(t)} - \tfrac{1}{2}A\rho\,\Delta t ,
\]
which the code applies after each step. When $u$ falls below $3u_{\mathrm{floor}}$ (for the helium plasma, $\mu = 4/3$, about $6.7 \times 10^{4}$ K) the particle becomes type $5$ and is collisionless from then on (Premise S3).

title: Time integration and output
text:
All particles share one time step,
\[
\Delta t = \min\Bigl(\Delta t_{\max},\ \min_{i}\tfrac{1}{4}\sqrt{\epsilon/|\mathbf{a}_{i}|},\ \min_{i\in\text{fluid}}\tfrac{1}{4}h_{i}/v_{\mathrm{sig},i}\Bigr),\qquad
v_{\mathrm{sig},i} = \max\Bigl(2c_{i},\ \max_{j}\bigl(c_{i} + c_{j} - 3w_{ij}\bigr)\Bigr),
\]
with $\Delta t_{\max} = 0.002$, the inner maximum over approaching pairs, and $w_{ij} = \mathbf{v}_{ij}\cdot\mathbf{r}_{ij}/r_{ij}$, negative on approach. The integrator is kick-drift-kick leapfrog, with the step shortened to land on each output time. Snapshots record positions, velocities, masses, internal energies, densities, smoothing lengths, types and halo labels. A merger run takes $15$ to $60$ minutes on two cores.

title: Time integration and output
text: \textbf{Tests.} Two tests (\file{tpsim\_tests.py}, output deposited) check the sheet fluid and the code's stability. A uniform sphere of hot sheet fluid ($2000$ particles) with every normal along $z$ grows in rms extent by factors $1.49$ and $1.47$ in $x$ and $y$ over $0.1$ time units and stays at $1.00$ in $z$; with random normals it grows by $1.33$ to $1.35$ along all three axes. An isolated main-cluster halo with the unit-ball composition as written ($20{,}000$ particles, every species) keeps its $10$ and $50$ percent mass radii within $1.3$ percent over $1$ time unit ($0.98$ Gyr).

title: Halos
text:
A halo of mass $M_{200}$ and concentration $c$ is a Hernquist sphere of the same mass inside $r_{200}$, with the scale length that matches the Navarro-Frenk-White inner profile \cite{Hernquist1990, NFW1997, SpringelDiMatteoHernquist2005}:
\[
r_{200} = \Bigl(\frac{GM_{200}}{100H_{0}^{2}}\Bigr)^{1/3},\qquad
a = \frac{r_{200}}{c}\sqrt{2\Bigl[\ln(1 + c) - \frac{c}{1 + c}\Bigr]},\qquad
M_{H} = M_{200}\Bigl(1 + \frac{a}{r_{200}}\Bigr)^{2},
\]
with $H_{0} = 70$ km/s/Mpc; the first is the radius inside which the mean density is $200$ times critical, and the last makes the Hernquist enclosed mass $M_{H}r^{2}/(r + a)^{2}$ equal $M_{200}$ at $r_{200}$. The sphere is truncated at $15a$, keeping $225/256$ of $M_{H}$. Positions are drawn from the enclosed-mass profile; each particle is then assigned a species at random in proportion to the species' mass fraction (Premise S5).

Collisionless particles take speeds from the isotropic Hernquist distribution function $f(E)$ \cite{Hernquist1990} by rejection sampling up to the escape speed, with random directions. Fluid particles start at rest with $u = \sigma_{r}^{2}/(\gamma - 1)$, so that $P = \rho\sigma_{r}^{2}$ and the gas is in hydrostatic equilibrium with the isotropic Jeans dispersion
\[
\sigma_{r}^{2}(r) = \frac{GM_{H}}{12a}\Bigl[12x(1 + x)^{3}\ln\frac{1 + x}{x} - \frac{x}{1 + x}\bigl(25 + 52x + 42x^{2} + 12x^{3}\bigr)\Bigr], \qquad x = r/a ,
\]
which solves $d(\rho\sigma_{r}^{2})/dr = -\rho\,GM(r)/r^{2}$ for the Hernquist density. The sheet fluid has no pressure along its normal, so it also carries a Gaussian velocity of dispersion $\sigma_{r}$ along the normal.

text:

The random-number seed is $7$ for every merger. Every halo has baryons $0.1571$ of its mass (galaxies $0.020$, our gas $0.1371$) and dark matter $0.8429$, split by composition as in the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.averaged-pair-operator}. title: Cluster assembly
text: Eight progenitors with $M_{200} = 2 \times 10^{14}\ \Msun$ and $c = 5$, $4000$ particles each, are placed at random inside $1.5$ Mpc, at least $700$ kpc apart, with random velocities of dispersion $150$ km/s, and the whole is set at rest at the origin. They collapse and merge into one cluster, $2.3 \times 10^{15}\ \Msun$ in all with $M_{200} \approx 2.0 \times 10^{15}\ \Msun$ at the end, followed to $t = 2.0$ ($1.96$ Gyr). Each composition in the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.merger} is run with two random seeds, $11$ and $23$; \texttt{rule1} is run once, with seed $11$ (projected ellipticity $0.17$, $0.72$ of CDM's with the same seed), and is not tabulated.

title: Measurements
text: \textbf{Centres.} Each cluster's centre is found by shrinking spheres on its own collisionless members (dark matter, galaxies and settled mirror matter): the centre of mass within a sphere, the sphere shrunk by $10$ percent, repeated down to $40$ kpc. The search at each snapshot starts from the previous one.

title: Measurements
text: \textbf{The Bullet-like moment.} The Bullet-like moment is the nearer of the two snapshots after closest approach that bracket the observed $720$ kpc separation, or the last snapshot ($t = 1.3$) if that separation is never reached.

title: Measurements
Measurements
text: \textbf{Halo shapes.} The assembled cluster's centre is found by shrinking spheres on all mass. Its three-dimensional axis ratios come from the iterative reduced inertia tensor, $I_{ab} = \sum m\,x_{a}x_{b}/r_{\mathrm{ell}}^{2}$ over the ellipsoid of the current shape, inside $300$ and $1000$ kpc. The projected ellipticity $1 - b/a$ is the same construction in two dimensions inside a projected $500$ kpc, averaged over the three coordinate projections; this is the quantity of Fact \claimref{simulations.imported-cluster-shapes}.

title: The merger
text:
In reading (W) the subcluster's sheet fluid and mirror gas are held back with its gas, $71$ percent of its mass ($56$ percent in the mixed count). Its potential collapses, its galaxies spread, and by the end of the runs it has not separated beyond $500$ to $630$ kpc. With random normals, or with the normals along the line of sight so that the merger axis lies in the sheets, it has no separate lensing peak (contrast $0.81$ to $0.95$). With every normal along this merger's axis (\texttt{rule\_par}) the fluid slides through along the axis; the subcluster then has a lensing peak (contrast $3.24$, $15$ kpc from its galaxies) but keeps half its mass. The mixed count fails in the same way. With the mirror collisionless from the start, so that only the sheet fluid collides, the subcluster keeps a weaker peak (contrast $2.69$ in the mixed count, $3.78$ with one three-dimensional tower colliding) and $0.44$ to $0.55$ of CDM's own mass: with a quarter to a third of the dark matter as sheet fluid, the sheet fluid alone costs about half the subcluster's central mass.

In reading (C) the subcluster reaches the observed separation with its mass peak on its galaxies and its gas $355$ kpc behind. Its own mass inside $150$ kpc of its galaxies is $0.57$ of CDM's, a deficit larger than the $23$ percent bound, because its halo puffs more than it strips. Its galaxies spread with it: the galaxy mass within $150$ kpc of the galaxy peak is $0.83$ of its start, where CDM's is compressed to $1.31$. Mass and light leave the aperture together, so the ratio inside it is kept while the mass inside it falls. Per unit of its collisionless content, the subcluster's collisionless matter inside the aperture is $0.683$ as concentrated as CDM's, and $0.683 \times 0.814$ (the collisionless share of the dark matter in reading (C), $1 - 0.186$) gives $0.556$, its collisionless matter against CDM's dark matter in the aperture; with stars and settled mirror matter the own mass is $0.57$. The mass-to-light ratio, from which the bound is derived, is therefore the test: its change is $0.82$ (the ratio itself $0.89$) against the observed $0.84 \pm 0.07$; CDM's is $0.87$ (ratio $1.00$). With a sampling error of $15$ to $21$ percent this measure does not separate reading (C) from CDM; the lensing peak and the gas offset separate both from reading (W). Its contrast, $4.7$ against CDM's $7.5$, is lower, and it has lost its mirror gas and part of its outer halo (a figure of the original). Each composition is one realisation of one geometry. Computed; observation level.

title: Halo shapes
text: Isolated assembly from eight progenitors makes rounder halos than infall along filaments, so the measure is the ratio to the CDM run (the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.merger}), and with two seeds the criterion is whether both seeds of a composition lie below both of CDM's. In reading (W) they do: the ellipticity is $0.43$ of CDM's (seed ratios $0.56$ and $0.35$), and the sheet fluid, supported by its pressure, is cored (its density is flat within the noise inside about $75$ kpc) and rounder than the collisionless dark matter (inside $300$ kpc, $c/a$ of $0.78$ and $0.85$ against $0.59$ and $0.44$ in the two seeds). It is also less concentrated: $38$ percent of the mass within $300$ kpc, near its measured share of $0.41$ within $r_{200}$, but only $10$ to $12$ percent inside $50$ kpc, where settled mirror matter is $39$ to $43$ percent. In reading (C) the ratio is $0.77$ ($0.63$ and $0.85$), and the second seed overlaps CDM's range: rounder, not excluded. Inside $300$ kpc in seed $11$ its $c/a$ matches CDM's ($0.62$ against $0.64$) and its $b/a$ is larger ($0.93$ against $0.71$), so the halo is closer to oblate symmetry than CDM's. In reading (C), $39$ and $29$ percent of the mass inside $50$ kpc (seeds $11$ and $23$) is settled mirror matter: the over-cooling of a dissipative gas simulated without feedback (Premise S3), which also makes the inner profiles unreliable. The compositions with the mirror settled from the start sit at $0.75$ to $0.78$ of CDM; at equal sheet fluid, the mixed count with its mirror gas gives $0.49$ and without it $0.75$, and the mirror gas without sheet fluid, reading (C), gives $0.77$: the mirror gas and the sheet fluid together round the halo more than either alone. Computed; observation level.

title: Cluster assembly
text: A halo-model estimate of the small-scale matter power spectrum, with the simulated change of profile applied at every mass (\file{pk.py}, output deposited), gives $P(k)/P_{\mathrm{CDM}} = 1.01$ to $1.34$ at $k$ of about $3$ and $10\ h\,\mathrm{Mpc^{-1}}$ for the unit-ball, mixed and reading (C) halos. The seed-to-seed spread is as large as the effect, so the test is not used.

title: The films
text:
Both films are rendered from simulation snapshots by \file{render\_lib.py} \cite{ButlerSuppT14b}. Each layer is a projected map along the line of sight on a grid of $300$ cells across the field, smoothed by a Gaussian of $18$ kpc (gas) or $25$ kpc (total mass), placed on a log scale, and added in its own colour onto a dark ground: galaxies as individual points, our gas weighted by $m\rho\sqrt{u}$ (a bremsstrahlung proxy for the X-ray map), mirror gas, and total projected mass as contours (what lensing measures). In Film 1 the sheet fluid is drawn as solid green contours rather than a fill, since a green fill screen-blended over the pink gas reads as white. The colour scales are fixed from one snapshot and shared by every panel, so brightness can be compared across panels.

The films use the same initial conditions as the runs of the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.averaged-pair-operator}, re-run with snapshots every $0.01$ time units ($9.8$ Myr). They reproduce the Bullet-moment measurements of the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.averaged-pair-operator} within run-to-run noise (contrast $4.48$ against $4.74$ for (C), $0.92$ against $0.95$ for (W), $7.27$ against $7.50$ for CDM; mass-to-light change $0.79$ against $0.82$ for (C)), the differences coming from the shifted time steps.

title: The films
text:
\textbf{Film 1: the merger, three ways.} \file{merger\_three\_ways.mp4} ($16$ s, $1920 \times 1080$), titled for a general audience ``Galaxy clusters in collision: testing three ideas about dark matter'', shows CDM, reading (W) with random normals and reading (C) side by side from approach to $1.27$ Gyr, labelled ``Standard cold dark matter: none of it collides'', ``Unit-ball rule: mirror and 3D-tower matter collide'' and ``Unit-ball rule: only mirror matter collides''.

The subtitle states that collisions are within a tower's own matter and that different towers interact only through gravity (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}). Collisionless matter appears only in the total-mass contours, so the CDM panel has no orange or green layer and the right-hand panel no green one; the film's legend calls the sheet fluid ``colliding 3D-tower matter''. A panel beside the chart explains the Bullet-like separation.

Below the maps a chart, with its own legend, follows the subcluster's own mass (a figure of the original), with a cursor at the current time. The film runs without pauses; reading (C)'s Bullet-like separation, $1.17$ Gyr, falls at $15$ s. The camera is centred between the two clusters of the CDM run and its width follows their separation; positions are interpolated linearly between snapshots at three frames per interval.

title: The films
text: \textbf{Film 2: the Bullet-like moment.} \file{bullet\_moment.mp4} ($20$ s, $1600 \times 900$) uses the snapshot of reading (C)'s run in the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.averaged-pair-operator} at $t = 1.20$ ($1.17$ Gyr). It adds the layers one at a time (galaxies, our gas, mirror gas, total mass) with a sentence on each, then marks the subcluster's galaxy peak, its mass peak, its gas peak and the main cluster's mass peak, and lists the simulated values beside the observed ones of Fact \claimref{simulations.imported-bullet-cluster}: separation $729$ kpc against $720$; mass peak $5$ kpc from the galaxies against about $42$ kpc, within $1\sigma$; gas $355$ kpc behind against an $8\sigma$ offset; mass-to-light $0.82 \pm 0.17$ against $0.84 \pm 0.07$ (the film shows the change since $t = 0$ with its $21$ percent sampling error, the section ``Measurements''); contrast $4.7$, with CDM's $7.5$ for reference.

title: The mirror in the Galaxy
text: The mirror's share is the same in both readings, so the merger cannot separate them. Its standing test in T14 is the Galaxy \cite[\S 8, refutation item 6]{ButlerT14}: dissipative mirror matter, $18.6$ percent of the dark matter, must not settle into structures the Milky Way's dynamics excludes.

title: Composition and recombination
text: With $\xi$ in T14's interval the mirror's weak interactions freeze out at $T' = 274$, $117$ and $47$ MeV for $\xi = 2.8 \times 10^{-4}$, $10^{-3}$ and $4 \times 10^{-3}$ (rate normalised to our freeze-out at $0.80$ MeV, expansion set by our $g_{*} = 106.75$). T14 gives $0.43$ to $0.45$ GeV at the floor; both lie above the hadronisation temperature, so the helium fraction is the same. Near the floor the neutron-to-proton ratio is set at hadronisation, so $Y' = 0.996$, $0.995$ and $0.986$: helium, with $0.4$ to $1.4$ percent residual hydrogen. Saha recombination of helium at $\eta'$, with $\xi$ raised by T14's entropy factor of about $2.6$ after burning (and by its burning reheat, a further factor of about $3.1$, at the floor), puts it at a visible temperature of $0.08$ to $1.6$ keV, redshift $3 \times 10^{5}$ to $7 \times 10^{6}$, overlapping T14's $0.1$ to $0.8$ keV \cite[Prop.~4.6]{ButlerT14}; the ends differ by the recombination criterion and the reheating bracket, which does not affect what follows. The extra radiation is $\Delta N_{\mathrm{eff}} \le 10^{-7}$. After recombination the mirror gas has a Jeans mass of $2 \times 10^{-6}$ to $2 \times 10^{-4}\ \Msun$ at $z = 100$: for the cosmic microwave background and large-scale structure it is cold dark matter, and the Galaxy is where it can be tested.

title: Cooling
The model
text:
One Milky Way halo is shared by both sectors: the same growth, potential and spin. Its growth follows the Fakhouri-Ma-Boylan-Kolchin rate \cite{Fakhouri2010},
\[
\frac{dM}{dt} = A\Bigl(\frac{M}{10^{12}\Msun}\Bigr)^{1.1}(1 + bz)\sqrt{\Omega_{m}(1+z)^{3} + \Omega_{\Lambda}},
\]
with $(A, b) = (46.1\ \Msun/\mathrm{yr}, 1.11)$ (mean) or $(25.3, 1.65)$ (median). Each sector accretes its baryon share $f_{b}\,dM$ ($f_{b} = \Omega_{b}/\Omega_{m} = 0.1565$) into a hot halo, an isothermal sphere $\rho_{g}(r) = m_{\mathrm{hot}}/(4\pi Rr^{2})$ at the virial temperature $T = \mu m_{p}V^{2}/2k$ of its own composition. Following Croton et al.\ \cite{Croton2006}, with their parameter values, and with $R$ and $V$ the halo's virial radius and circular velocity, $m_{\mathrm{hot}}$ and $m_{\mathrm{cold}}$ the hot and cold gas masses, $r_{\mathrm{cool}}$ the radius at which the cooling time equals the reference time, and $\lambda$ the spin parameter:
\begin{align*}
t_{\mathrm{cool}}(r_{\mathrm{cool}}) &= t_{\mathrm{dyn}} = R/V \quad (\text{or the cosmic time}),\\
\dot m_{\mathrm{cool}} &= \tfrac{1}{2}m_{\mathrm{hot}}\frac{r_{\mathrm{cool}}}{R}\frac{V}{R} \quad (\text{all hot gas per } t_{\mathrm{dyn}} \text{ if } r_{\mathrm{cool}} > R),\\
\dot m_{*} &= \alpha\,\frac{m_{\mathrm{cold}} - m_{\mathrm{crit}}}{t_{\mathrm{disk}}}, \qquad
m_{\mathrm{crit}} = 3.8 \times 10^{9}\Msun\,\frac{V}{200\ \mathrm{km/s}}\,\frac{3R_{d}}{10\ \kpc},\\
\Delta m_{\mathrm{reheat}} &= \epsilon_{\mathrm{disk}}F\,\Delta m_{*}, \qquad
\Delta E = \tfrac{1}{2}\epsilon_{\mathrm{halo}}F\,\Delta m_{*}V_{\mathrm{SN}}^{2},\\
\Delta m_{\mathrm{eject}} &= \frac{\Delta E - \tfrac{1}{2}\Delta m_{\mathrm{reheat}}V^{2}}{\tfrac{1}{2}V^{2}}, \qquad
\dot m_{\mathrm{return}} = \gamma_{\mathrm{ej}}\,m_{\mathrm{ej}}/t_{\mathrm{dyn}},
\end{align*}
with $\alpha = 0.07$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{disk}} = 3.5$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{halo}} = 0.35$, $V_{\mathrm{SN}} = 630$ km/s, $\gamma_{\mathrm{ej}} = 0.5$, recycled fraction $0.43$, $R_{d} = \lambda R/\sqrt{2}$ and $t_{\mathrm{disk}} = 3R_{d}/V$. Metals are followed in each sector from a metal-free start: a yield $y = 0.03$ per unit of stars formed enters the cold gas and is carried by every flow, and each hot halo cools at its own metallicity. The feedback factor $F$ multiplies the supernova energy and mass loading per unit stellar mass; for our sector it is a calibrated number $F_{\mathrm{cal}}$, and the mirror's is $F$ times that.

title: The model
text:
\textbf{Calibration and normalisation.} In each set-up our sector's $F_{\mathrm{cal}}$ is tuned so that its settled mass, stars plus cold gas, is the observed $6.0 \times 10^{10}\ \Msun$. The mirror, at $\Omega_{b'} = 0.995\,\Omega_{b}$, then runs in the same halo with feedback $F\,F_{\mathrm{cal}}$ and with yield $yF$ (its extra feedback comes from extra supernovae, which also make metals; the consistent choice) or, for comparison, $y$. Its surface density at the Sun is normalised to ours, either in total,
\[
\Sigma'_{x} = 47.1\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}\times\frac{m'_{x}}{6.0 \times 10^{10}\ \Msun},
\]
or with gas and stars scaled separately to our observed $13.7$ and $33.4$ (component normalisation). The mass the mirror puts in the bulge volume is taken as a quarter of its settled mass, the fraction of ours the bulge volume holds. There are $24$ set-ups: $M_{200} = 1.0$, $1.2$ and $1.5 \times 10^{12}\ \Msun$; mean or median growth; $t_{\mathrm{dyn}}$ or cosmic time as cooling reference; and a star-formation-threshold disk of $5.6$ kpc ($\lambda = 0.035$) or $2.6$ kpc ($\lambda = 0.0163$, the Milky Way's). Points with $F\,F_{\mathrm{cal}}$ above $12$ are dropped as not converged.

title: How much feedback a helium mirror has
text:
A pure-helium star is a bare helium core. Helium stars collapse to iron cores from about $2.5\ \Msun$ \cite{Woosley2019}, form black holes above final masses of about $10$ to $12\ \Msun$ \cite{Woosley2019, Ertl2020}, and explode by pair instability from $64$ to $133\ \Msun$ \cite{HegerWoosley2002}. Taking $10^{50}$ erg from $2.5$ to $3\ \Msun$, $10^{51}$ erg from $3\ \Msun$ to the black-hole cut, none above it to $64\ \Msun$, and pair-instability energies rising from $10^{51}$ to $10^{53}$ erg, the energy per unit mass formed relative to ours ($1.08 \times 10^{49}$ erg/$\Msun$ for a Chabrier IMF \cite{Chabrier2003}, one core collapse per $93\ \Msun$) is given in the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.halo-shapes}.

title: The mirror in the Galaxy
text:
Over the $24$ set-ups:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] The proton-only branch, at the feedback a hydrogen population has ($F = 1$), puts $47$ to $56\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ of gas and stars at the Sun and $(15$ to $18) \times 10^{9}\ \Msun$ in the bulge volume. It fails every combination of bounds and normalisations.
\item[(ii)] The helium branch without star formation settles $48$ to $117\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$. It fails.
\item[(iii)] The helium branch with stars at $F = 1$ gives $23$ to $42\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ and $(7$ to $13) \times 10^{9}\ \Msun$. It fails. At equal feedback it settles $49$ to $85$ percent as much as our sector, because it cools more slowly.
\item[(iv)] The helium branch at the helium-star feedback, $F = 3.6$ to $7.3$ with yield $yF$, gives $5.6$ to $20\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ of gas and stars, $1$ to $8$ of gas, and $(1.8$ to $6.2) \times 10^{9}\ \Msun$ in the bulge volume; with yield $y$, $4.2$ to $14$, $1$ to $7$ and $(1.3$ to $4.2) \times 10^{9}\ \Msun$. Whether it passes depends on choices the data and the model do not fix. The first is how much of the bulge's dark mass, $3.1 \times 10^{9}\ \Msun$ (Fact \claimref{simulations.imported-milky-ways-mass-budget}), may be mirror: $0.6 \times 10^{9}$ if it is shared in proportion to the composition, $3.1 \times 10^{9}$ if the collisionless towers contribute nothing there, up to $8.3 \times 10^{9}$ if a mirror bar can hide within the stellar mass-to-light uncertainty. Every floor computed here exceeds $0.6 \times 10^{9}$, so on the proportional reading the bulge excludes the helium branch at every $F$ and yield; it survives in the bulge only on the other two, which require over twice the proportional share ($1.33/0.6 = 2.2$ times with yield $y$, $1.78/0.6 = 3.0$ with $yF$): held as dark mass, over $43$ percent of the bulge's dark mass with yield $y$ and $57$ percent with $yF$; otherwise hidden within the stellar mass-to-light uncertainty. The others are the normalisation of the mirror's gas, the bounds at the Sun, the yield and the IMF.

With yield $yF$, the numbers of converged set-ups that pass the lenient bounds at the Sun (thin gas below $5.59$, gas and stars below $15\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$) and each reading of the bulge room are as follows, given as ranges over the two black-hole cuts and the two disk scales (\file{verdict\_output.txt} has every count):

title: The result
text:
So with the consistent yield the Galaxy test would be decided by either of two measurements not yet made: a $2\sigma$ limit below $5\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ on extra disk-like mass at the Sun with scale height $100$ to $500$ pc (the room is $4.6 \pm 5$, the dynamical stellar surface density less the counted one, Fact \claimref{simulations.imported-milky-ways-mass-budget}), or a limit below $1.7 \times 10^{9}\ \Msun$ on disk-like dark mass in the bulge volume, which would bound the mirror's mass there directly, whatever reading of the room is taken. Either excludes the helium branch under every choice tried with yield $yF$; with the yield held at ours the limits would need to reach $4.2\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ and $1.3 \times 10^{9}\ \Msun$. The thin-gas bound is not used to decide, because the mirror's gas at high $F$ sits at the star-formation threshold of the model, which is its least certain part.

Roux and Cline find $\Omega_{b'} \lesssim 0.8\,\Omega_{b}$ at low mirror temperature \cite{RouxCline2020}. Their analysis includes a helium mirror with $\eta' = \eta\,\beta/x^{3}$, down to $x = T'/T = 10^{-3}$, which covers T14's hot end; what it does not include is the floor of T14's interval and the helium-star supernova factor.

title: What the tests decide, and what they cost
text: \textbf{What the tests decide.} Read as T14 writes it, the composition fails the merger and the halo shapes, and it fails them because of the three-dimensional towers' self-interaction, not because of the amounts. Read with the odd towers collisionless, the same amounts keep a lensing peak on the subcluster's galaxies with its gas behind and a mass-to-light change consistent with the observed ratio (as CDM's is; the measure does not discriminate), and come within a quarter of CDM on halo shapes. The remaining exposure is the mirror in the Galaxy, the same in both readings: its helium branch is open at the Sun, at the $2\sigma$ room, under some normalisations of the mirror's gas and, in the bulge, only if the bulge holds over twice the mirror's proportional share of its dark mass.

title: What the tests decide, and what they cost
text:
\textbf{Statements of T14 the tests bear on.} T14 records the outcome in its Section 7.7 and at each place cited below \cite[Fact~7.32]{ButlerT14}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item At composite strength the three-dimensional towers' self-interaction is $10^{8}$ to $10^{13}\ \cmg$ (Proposition \claimref{simulations.effective-cross-section-sheet-matter}), far above the cluster bounds \cite[Prop.~6.2]{ButlerT14}.
\item ``A halo built from collisionless sheets is a cold-dark-matter halo'' \cite[Rem.~7.30]{ButlerT14} needs the sheet matter collisionless; as a fluid it is cored, rounder and less concentrated than collisionless matter (Observation \claimref{simulations.halo-shapes}).
\item The self-interacting fraction, counted as all colliding dark matter, is $68$ percent in reading (W) and $19$ percent in reading (C); T14's Proposition 7.15(v) counts the three-dimensional towers alone (about half); for the merger bound its Section 7.7 adds the mirror, as here \cite[Prop.~7.15(v), \S7.7]{ButlerT14}. The Bullet bound on mass loss is about $23$ percent \cite{Randall2008}, inferred from the mass-to-light ratio.
\item The mirror analysis T14 cites \cite[\S 8, refutation item 6]{ButlerT14} rescales $\eta$ and includes a helium mirror down to $T'/T = 10^{-3}$ \cite{RouxCline2020}; it covers the hot end of T14's interval, not its floor.
\item For the helium branch with stars the excess over the Galaxy's room at the Sun is a factor of $1.5$ to $2.8$ over the $2\sigma$ room of $15\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ at equal feedback, and at the helium-star feedback it falls within the $2\sigma$ room at the Sun in most set-ups in total normalisation (all of them at the best-shifted IMF) and persists in the bulge unless the bulge holds over twice the mirror's proportional share of its dark mass (Observation \claimref{simulations.mirror-galaxy}). The order-of-magnitude excess holds for the proton-only branch and for a mirror that forms no stars \cite[\S 8, refutation item 6]{ButlerT14}.
\item The current bounds on the settled phase are the thin-disk bound of Widmark et al.\ \cite{Widmark2021} and the microlensing bound of Mr\'oz et al.\ (compact objects at most $1$ percent of the halo from $1.8 \times 10^{-4}$ to $6.3\ \Msun$ and $10$ percent up to $860\ \Msun$ \cite{Mroz2024}), which T14's refutation item 6 uses. The thin-disk bound, about $5\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ at $95$ percent, holds for scale heights of $50$ pc or less; it does not reach the $5\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ at $100$ to $500$ pc that would decide the helium branch, and the bulge models \cite{Portail2017} do not separate a disk-like part of the bulge's dark mass, so the Galaxy test is not yet decidable.
\end{enumerate}

title: What the tests decide, and what they cost
Position in the series
text: This paper is T14b of the series, a companion to the dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14}. It is downstream of T14's Proposition 4.1 (superselection), Theorem 4.3 and Proposition 4.6 (the mirror), Proposition 6.2 (the radiation audit and its self-interaction statement) and Section 7 (the unit-ball rule, its premises R1 to R3, the thickness family and the moving sheets), and it tests the composition T14's Section 7 fixes against the record. Remark \claimref{note.simulations.what-premise-c-needs} refers to the Standard-Model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} for the gauge charges of the four-dimensional minimal massive composite. It proves nothing about the series' algebra and changes no derived result of T14; it says which of T14's physical statements the simulations and the Galaxy model support and which they do not (the section ``What the tests decide, and what they cost''). The capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17} should carry the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.mirror-galaxy} beside T14's ledger entry, Premise C as the condition under which the rule's composition meets the cluster record, and the two measurements of the section ``The mirror in the Galaxy'' that would decide the mirror's helium branch.

title: Machine verification
text:
\textbf{The script.} \file{verify\_T14b.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT14b} imports the series' shared library \file{GA.py} and checks the note's computational identities and derived numbers: $60$ checks, all passing, in eight parts. A few are arithmetic restatements of a quoted number rather than tests of a claim (D4, F3, R4, R7). Algebraic identities are checked in exact rational arithmetic; evaluations with physical constants, transcendental functions and integrals in double precision, with the tolerance stated beside each check.

\emph{Part A: composition.} $T(1) = (11\pi + 16)/(3\pi)$ between rational bounds; $T(\pi/2) = T(1)$; the three shares and their sum; the baryon, galaxy and gas fractions of every halo; the three colliding shares and their order against the bounds.

\emph{Part B: self-interaction.} Proposition \claimref{simulations.effective-cross-section-sheet-matter} as an exact identity; $n_{b}$ and $d_{b}$; the ratio $V_{3}/V_{2} = 4/3$ from the unit-ball volumes; the range of the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.effective-cross-section-sheet-matter}; the bound on $\lambda$; Computation \claimref{simulations.cluster-bound-two-dimensions}, with Bessel functions by their series; the five-dimensional range; the mean free path.

\emph{Part C: the code's algebra.} The kernel's normalisation, derivative and continuity, exactly; Lemma \claimref{simulations.averaged-pair-operator}(ii) in the blade engine of $\Cl(3,0)$, (iii) in exact rationals, including $P_{ij}^{2} \ne P_{ij}$ for orthogonal normals, and (i) on a rational instance with distinct normals and viscosity; the cooling update as a polynomial identity; the units; the settling threshold at $\mu = 0.6$ and its temperature for the helium plasma, from the code's $u(T)$ formula and constants; the algebra of the bremsstrahlung coefficient (the electron and ion densities and $T(u)$ for He$^{++}$) against $du/dt = -\varepsilon/\rho$, with the code's constants.

\emph{Part D: initial conditions.} The Hernquist matching and $r_{200}$, exactly; the Jeans equation for $\sigma_{r}^{2}$ at three radii; the truncation fraction; the merger geometry, exactly.

\emph{Part E: the mirror's composition.} Freeze-out temperatures, $Y'$, $\eta'$, the recombination temperature and $\Delta N_{\mathrm{eff}}$.

\emph{Part F: cooling.} The metal-free $\Lambda_{N}$ at three temperatures; the cooling-time ratios of helium to our gas; the Tozzi-Norman conversion.

\emph{Part G: supernova energy.} The continuity of the IMF; our energy per unit mass; $F$ for our IMF's shape and the best shifted IMF.

\emph{Part R: recorded outputs.} Selected simulation and model outputs, carried as constants from the run summaries, and the comparisons the text draws from them: the mass-to-light change, ratio and sampling error; the merger separations; the halo ratios, with their seed-paired values; the Galaxy floors against the decisive limits and the three readings of the bulge room. The outputs themselves are reproduced by the deposited scripts, not by this one: Part R does not read \file{outputs/}, so a change to a deposited output would not fail the script.

\emph{What the script does not check:} the simulations and the Galaxy model themselves, which the section ``Running the code'' shows how to rerun, and the imported Facts and published bounds.

    tests/                  the two code tests
    sims/                   runs/<tag>/ (mergers) and halos/<tag>/ (assembly)
    films/                  runs/<tag>/ (film re-runs, compact frames)
    galaxy/                 the Galaxy model's outputs
    outputs/                regenerated results, named as in outputs/
    figures/                regenerated figures
  work_quick/             created by reproduce.py --quick, laid out as work/
\end{verbatim}}
Two rules follow from how the scripts are written. First, every file in \file{code/} must stay in that one folder: the scripts import one another by module name (\file{ics}, \file{render\_lib}, \file{sam2} and so on), and Python finds them because they sit beside the script being run. Second, the working directory matters. The simulation and measurement scripts read and write paths relative to the folder they are run from (\file{runs/}, \file{halos/}, \file{./tpsim}), so they must be run from \file{work/sims} (mergers, assembly, measurements) or \file{work/films} (film re-runs), never from \file{code/}. \file{reproduce.py} sets the working directory for each stage and copies \file{tpsim} into place, so the simplest course is to run everything through it.

title: Laying out the files
text: \textbf{In an IDE.} In Visual Studio Code, open \file{T14b\_supplement} with \emph{File, Open Folder} (on Windows, from inside WSL with the WSL extension's \emph{Open Folder in WSL}). \textbf{Single runs by hand.} Compile \file{tpsim} and copy it into the stage folder, then run from there:

mkdir -p work/bin work/sims
gcc -O3 -fopenmp -o work/bin/tpsim code/tpsim.c -lm
cp work/bin/tpsim work/sims/
cd work/sims
python ../../code/merger.py mirror random mirror_only

python ../../code/analyze3.py cdm mirror_only
\end{verbatim}}
\file{merger.py} takes a model, a sheet orientation and a run name, then optionally the particle numbers of the two clusters (default $60{,}000$ and $20{,}000$) and an end time (capped at $1.3$). The models are \texttt{cdm}, \texttt{rule}, \texttt{mixed}, \texttt{mixednm}, \texttt{rule1}, \texttt{rule1nm} and \texttt{mirror} (the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.averaged-pair-operator}); the orientations are \texttt{random}, \texttt{perp} and \texttt{par}. \file{halo.py} takes a model, \texttt{random}, a run name, then particles per progenitor, end time and seed; the note's runs used $4000$, $2.0$ and seeds $11$ and $23$ (the defaults are $5000$, $2.5$ and $11$). \file{analyze3.py} measures the named merger runs and should be given \texttt{cdm} first, since own mass is relative to it. \file{tpsim} itself takes the initial-conditions file, an output prefix, the end time, the snapshot interval, the softening, the opening angle $\theta$, the cooling coefficient $A$, the energy floor, and optionally $\Delta t_{\max}$ and $h_{\min}$; the scripts pass $0.02$ (mergers) or $0.5$ (assembly), $15$, $0.7$, \texttt{ics.cooling\_A()}, \texttt{ics.u\_of\_T(1e4)}, $0.002$ and $10$.

title: What to expect
The mirror share is one, and how fragile that is
text:
Write $m_{r} = c_{r}\Lambda_{r}$, with $\Lambda_{r}$ the confinement scale of tower $r$'s non-abelian sector and $c_{r}$ the constituent factor of its lightest charge-carrying composite.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The mirror.)} By Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iii), $\Lambda_{2} = \Lambda_{6}$ and $c_{2} = c_{6}$ exactly, hence $f_{2} = 1$ under P4, which Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v) discharges for the mirror, an isomorphism of theories rather than a one-loop statement. As a ratio of mass densities it is a ratio of mean mass per baryon: ours is about $936.7$ MeV after helium, a mirror burnt entirely to helium (the completion limit of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}'s burning branch) gives $931.8$ MeV, so $f_{2}$ is $0.995$ in that limit and $1$ on the proton-only branch, a one-sided systematic of half a percent at assembly level. Caveat (T14c): the two branches bracket the share where the mirror is helium or protons; at the gravitational floor the mirror is degenerate and, for a copied lepton number $L \leq 0$, ends $96$ to $100$ percent neutrons, a composition neither branch describes, and it is helium only for $\xi$ between about $3 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2 \times 10^{-2}$ (Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition}); the half-percent bracket is established there and not at the floor.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Fragility.)} The equality is unstable to any departure from the copy. Suppose the two towers shared a ceiling $M$ and coupling but differed in light content by $\Delta b$ over the running range, with $b_{6} \leq 11$; then at one loop
\[
\ln\frac{\Lambda_{2}}{\Lambda_{6}} \;\geq\; \frac{\Delta b}{b_{6} + \Delta b}\,\ln\frac{M}{\Lambda_{6}}.
\]
One Dirac flavour is $\Delta b = 2/3$, which with $\Lambda_{6} = 0.3$ GeV moves the mirror share by a factor between $4.89$ (bottom of the ceiling range, $b_{6} = 11$) and $21.4$ (top, $b_{6} = 7$), past the observed $5.364$ everywhere except at the bottom of the range on the most conservative branch. A coupling departure $\delta = \alpha_{2}(M)^{-1} - \alpha_{6}(M)^{-1}$ at the ceiling with identical content moves $\Lambda_{2}/\Lambda_{6}$ by $e^{-2\pi\delta/b}$, a factor $2.45$ per unit at $b = 7$, so the share stays within ten percent of one only for $|\delta| < 0.106$. So $f_{2} = 1$ is exact, P2-protected, and fragile.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The odd towers.)} In three and five dimensions the gauge coupling is dimensionful and the confinement scale is set by the coupling itself ($\Lambda_{3} \sim g_{3}^{2}N$, $\Lambda_{5} \sim 1/g_{5}^{2}$), so nothing about $\Lambda_{1,7,3,5}$ follows without a rule the series does not derive (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}); the unit-ball rule of the section ``The dark matter ratio: the unit-ball rule'' constrains that rule, as shares per unit of our volume, without supplying it.
\end{enumerate}
Level: (i) is Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}; (ii) is one-loop arithmetic under its stated assumptions, flagged; (iii) is a scope statement.

title: The radiation audit: what the type-by-residue theorem closes, and what stays open
text:
The cosmic microwave background caps extra relativistic energy at $\Delta\Neff \lesssim 0.3$ \cite{Planck2018}, and one massless photon-like species (two polarisations) at the visible temperature contributes $\Delta\Neff = (8/7)(11/4)^{4/3} \approx 4.4$, so five democratically filled sectors with such photons would contribute of order twenty. The audit proceeds tower by tower, at two levels fixed by Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can} and Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.where-flag-defined-what-it-carries}: the \emph{ground} level, where the type decides whether the tower's spinors carry an intrinsic $U(1)$ (exactly at the complex member of each odd pair, $r = 3, 7$ in the paper's convention), and the \emph{rung} level, where every flagged tower carries abelian charges from its ladder pairs.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The mirror tower, $r = 2$.)} Open, by theorem: the mirror's derived content is a copy of ours (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}), so it has a massless mirror photon and three light mirror neutrinos. The ground level is closed for the real member of the pair $\{2, 6\}$ (intrinsic group $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$, Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}(i); which member depends on the labelling convention, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}) and irrelevant, since the content is not at that level. This is the mirror-matter situation of the literature, costed in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs}.
\item \emph{(The three-dimensional towers, $r = 1, 7$.)} Closed at both levels: vector-like (no chirality in odd dimension), so Dirac masses are unforbidden and generic; with no massless charged matter left, each compact $U(1)$ in three dimensions, the intrinsic one of the complex member of $\{1, 7\}$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}(ii)) and the rung-level ones of both, leaves no massless photon. The paper states that every such $U(1)$ confines by monopoles \cite{Polyakov1977}; with the half-integral bare Chern-Simons level that the parity anomaly forces (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.anomalies}(i)), that holds in the confining phase (C) only, and in phase (T) the photon is instead topologically massive (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-phases}); both phases close the channel. The non-abelian factors confine.
\item \emph{(The five-dimensional towers, $r = 3, 5$.)} Open at both levels: the complex member of the pair $\{3, 5\}$ carries an intrinsic $U(1)$ by theorem (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}(ii); which member depends on the convention), both carry rung-level ones, no Polyakov mechanism exists in five dimensions, and by Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} a surviving photon dilutes as $a^{-4}$, exactly as ours.
\item \emph{(The Goldstone exposure.)} Confining dark sectors with chiral breaking could leave massless dark pions. The framework supplies its own gap: any tower's accidental global symmetries are broken by its own tower's higher rungs (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}), so the Goldstones are pseudo-Goldstones with masses of order $\Lambda_{\mathrm{conf}}^{2}/M_{\mathrm{rung}}$, the existence input a theorem and the mass estimate dimensional analysis.
\end{enumerate}
Conclusion: the three-dimensional towers are closed by theorem plus Polyakov confinement or, in phase (T), topological mass; the mirror tower is open by theorem, with a known relativistic content, and closes only if it is cold, which by Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2} is an exception to P2 (applied with the reach of Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv), (v), P2 gives $\xi = 1$ and $\Delta\Neff = 7.45$); the five-dimensional towers are open with a content this paper does not derive. By the section ``Seeding by gravity, and why no coupling rule follows'' (proved given the imported rate) every dark tower's temperature is bounded below by gravitational heating at a few parts in ten thousand of the visible temperature at the top of the ceiling range, and above by whatever energy the descent deposited, which the $\Neff$ cap limits to $0.448$ for the mirror and the paper's hot-deposit estimate puts near $4 \times 10^{-3}$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}); across that interval both the mirror's channel and the five-dimensional towers' close by eight orders or more (twelve at the floor; the one case below eight is a nine-vector tower at the hot end, at $7.4$). $\Delta\Neff \approx 0$ is therefore a conditional stance, conditional on the open channels closing by one of the routes of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs} and on the deposit being no hotter than the estimate; so registered, and stated with that cost.

On self-interaction: in the three-dimensional towers it is at composite strength if their matter is the confined charged matter the closure leaves, which the series does not establish (the section ``The composition in galaxy clusters and in the Galaxy''); in the five-dimensional ones it is undetermined; and for the mirror the composite figure is the wrong one, since mirror matter recombines at a visible temperature of order a keV (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}) and enters structure formation as neutral mirror atoms, with an elastic cross-section per mass of order $2 \times 10^{8}$ (hydrogen) or $5 \times 10^{7}$ (helium) $\mathrm{cm^{2}\,g^{-1}}$, and as a plasma once ionised inside a halo: collisional and dissipative like our gas, tested by the collisional-fraction and dark-disk bounds of refutation item 6. The rung-breaking scale of channel (4) is valued in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.ceiling-valued-inherited-success}.

title: A reduced response to gravity needs a supporting stress; the sheets move
text:
Let a pressureless component respond to the gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}; the perturbed FLRW field in the conformal Newtonian gauge of Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-linear-momentum-equation-traceless-field}, potentials $\psi$, $\phi$) at a fraction $g$ of the full strength, $\theta' = -\mathcal{H}\theta + g\,k^{2}\psi$. Then (i) it carries the anisotropic stress $\sigma = (1 - g)\psi$, and no other value; (ii) that stress enters the field equations, so that with the other components' stresses $\Sigma$,
\[
\psi \;=\; \frac{\phi - 12\pi G a^{2}\Sigma/k^{2}}{1 + 12\pi G a^{2}\rho\,(1 - g)/k^{2}} .
\]
For a three-dimensional tower whose sheets are held fixed, $g = \sin^{2}\theta$ for a wavevector at angle $\theta$ to the missing direction (script: $k_{\perp}^{2}/k^{2}$), $\tfrac{2}{3}$ averaged over orientations, and the stress of (i) is that of a medium holding the sheets in place. The series supplies no such medium: nothing in Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} or in the towers' content gives the sheet family a rigidity along its normal, and the sourcing rule couples the sheets' matter to the one gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ like any other. Hence, on the series as written, the sheets are displaced along their normal by the potential gradient, $g = 1$, and the three-dimensional towers respond to gravity in full at linear order.

title: The stored asymmetry is a charge, not a number
text:
Under the classification of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fifteenth-refutation}, with $\epsilon$ initial data of the descent, inherited rather than generated, and the number $N$ common to the towers under P1 ($N = M_{P}/H$, which fixes the boundary mode count, about $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$, without being it: Observation \claimref{standard-model.largeness-number-universes-boundary-modes}; the argument uses only that $N$ is common):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Charge.)} The asymmetry stored in an oriented tower is the charge $Q = \epsilon N$, fixed by the descent's data and independent of the tower's temperature; it is not a thermal number $n - \bar{n} \propto g\,\mu T^{2}$. So the mirror share $f_{2} = 1$ holds at any mirror temperature: a cold mirror carries the same baryon charge as this tower in the same number of baryons, with negligible mirror radiation.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Origin.)} The charge is the descent's and cannot be produced afterwards: the one channel superselection leaves open, gravitational production from the visible plasma (the section ``Seeding by gravity, and why no coupling rule follows''), yields $1.8$ to $2.7 \times 10^{-15}$ mirror quanta per unit entropy at the ceiling reheating against the $8.7 \times 10^{-11}$ baryons per unit entropy that our baryon number requires, more than four orders too few even counting every produced quantum as a baryon. Black holes are a sink for $Q$, not a source (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}(iv), under P5): a mass-preserving rearrangement that erodes each tower's free baryon count and moves no share.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Temperature.)} Taken as a free datum of the descent, which by Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2} is an exception to P2 (applied with the reach of Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv), (v), P2 gives $\xi = 1$, which the record excludes), the mirror's temperature ratio $\xi = T'/T$ is bounded below by the gravitational floor, $\xi$ between $2.8$ and $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$ at the ceiling reheating (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity}(ii), the bracket the species-counting ambiguity; four parts in a thousand of this at the bottom of the ceiling range), and above by the $\Neff$ cap at $0.448$; a deposit of each unit of baryon number with energy of order the reheating temperature puts it at $\xi \approx 4 \times 10^{-3}$. The paper carries the whole interval. With $\eta = n_{B}/n_{\gamma} = 6.1 \times 10^{-10}$ here and equal baryon number,
\[
\eta' \;=\; \frac{\eta}{\xi^{3}}
\]
runs from $19$ to $26$ at the floor down to about $0.008$ at the hot deposit, crossing one at $\xi = \eta^{1/3} = 8.5 \times 10^{-4}$: at least $10^{7}$ times ours throughout, with $\Delta\Neff$ eight orders or more below the cap.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The two readings.)} The thermal reading would give $f_{2} \sim \xi_{2}^{3}$ instead, at most $0.090$ under the $\Neff$ cap ($0.448^{3}$) and $10^{-7}$ or less anywhere in the interval; the two readings cannot both hold, and the paper's own classification decides for the charge.
\end{enumerate}
Level: the classification is Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-trichotomy-descents-data}'s; the incompatibility is arithmetic. The mirror's nucleosynthesis, which is not a copy of ours and on which the burning branch of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile}(i) and the composition caveat of refutation item 6 rest, follows the proof, at assembly level. Caveat (T14c): the proof's thermal up-down ratio at freeze-out fails at the floor, where the mirror is degenerate and, for a copied lepton number $L \leq 0$, ends $96$ to $100$ percent neutrons; it is helium only for $\xi$ between about $3 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2 \times 10^{-2}$, an interval containing the hot-deposit estimate (Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition}). The burning branch is therefore not the floor's composition.

title: Superselected, hence dark and exactly stable
text:
By Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point} and the acoustic programme (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-gravity-only-coupling}, the series' acoustic no-go, at its mixed level: within the s-wave current algebra, with the sphere step conditional on the Indifference premise and the thermal state on premise (Q)), matter in a neighbouring tower gravitates on this metric and does nothing else observable at first order: dark by structural necessity, at that level. Stability is then not suppressed but exact, in three steps, the first of which is proved given the sector decomposition of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.frozen-phase-operators}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The tower charge $r$ is superselected in the frozen phase: frozen-phase operators are built from the one soldering and preserve its signature (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.residue-soldered-invariant-not-algebraic-one}), so portal matrix elements between residues vanish identically away from walls.
\item The walls are unreachable: singular loci ascend within-tower, since the completion adjoins exactly $(1,1)$ and preserves the residue (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}), while the mod-8 shadow walls that separate residues are displaced successively away from the physical region, by the wall-sequence theorem of the sheaf paper \cite[\S5]{ButlerT4}, under that theorem's hypotheses (a compact base and good couplings at every stage), carried here.
\item Therefore the only inter-tower event in the universe's history is the descent itself: the towers communicated once, at the origin, and have been in absolute mutual darkness but for weight ever since. The singular locus of a black hole is an inter-tower event for energy, as it already was for weight, and never for the residue of any quantum: energy crosses at the wall, the residue does not (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}).
\end{enumerate}
One residue is flagged at observation level: dark-tower matter crossing this tower's horizons carries superselected charge the four-dimensional boundary mode space cannot hold, which routes it into the tower-wise run of the singularity paper's ascend-then-descend structure \cite{ButlerT5}; the computation of that routing, with the mass range of its Gauss-law clause, is Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}.

title: The unit-ball rule
text:
Under R1 to R3, the share of a tower whose space has $D$ dimensions is $f = \tfrac{V_{3}}{V_{D}}$, and
\[
\frac{\Omega_{\mathrm{dark}}}{\Omega_{b}} \;=\; V_{3}\sum_{\text{dark }r}\frac{1}{V_{D_{r}}}
\;=\; \frac{V_{3}}{V_{3}} + 2\,\frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}} + 2\,\frac{V_{3}}{V_{4}}
\;=\; 1 + \frac{8}{3} + \frac{16}{3\pi} \;=\; \frac{11\pi + 16}{3\pi} \;=\; 5.36432\ldots
\]
against the observed $5.364 \pm 0.065$. The agreement is built in, not predicted: the relation was found by solving for the observed value, and its clauses were chosen with it known, and the closed form is one of fourteen equally simple candidates within the error bar (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}).

title: No indirect dark-sector signals
text: No indirect dark-sector signals: no decay products, since the tower charge is superselected, and annihilation products only at the rate of graviton exchange, suppressed by powers of $E/M_{P}$ on a charge-asymmetric relic.
